drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's tereifa of an animal that fell from the roof extend to one merely found below?
outcomeNote: A lemma and Rav Huna's limitation of it; no challenge is raised within this unit.

segments.he: נָפְלָה מִן הַגָּג, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הִנִּיחַ בְּהֵמָה לְמַעְלָה, וּבָא וּמְצָאָהּ לְמַטָּה – אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין מִשּׁוּם רִיסּוּקֵי אֵבָרִים.
segments.en: § The mishna states: An animal that «fell from the roof» is a tereifa, since its limbs may have been shattered. «Rav Huna says:» If one «left an animal above,» on the roof, «and he came» back «and found it below,» but did not see it fall, «one» need «not be concerned with regard to the shattering of limbs.» One may presume that it jumped intentionally and was not injured.

moves.summary: cites the mishna's clause about an animal that fell from the roof
moves.about: opening the discussion of the mishna's clause about an animal that fell from the roof

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא: הניח בהמה למעלה
moves.summary: limits the mishna to a witnessed fall: an animal merely found below raises no concern of shattered limbs
moves.about: that the mishna's concern for shattered limbs applies only to a fall actually witnessed; an animal merely found below is presumed to have come down of its own accord
